title: Review: Decrement stock when an order is placed

steps.text: Hi. This change teaches the inventory service to react to new orders, and adds a column for reserved stock. There are two issues I'd fix before merging, and two smaller ones.

Let's start with the migration. It adds a column that can't be null, but gives it no default. On Postgres, that fails as soon as the table has any rows. It will work on an empty dev database and then break in production. Adding a default of zero fixes it.

Now the consumer. Messages can be delivered more than once, but this handler decrements stock every time it runs. So a single retry means the order is counted twice. Keep a record of processed events, in the same transaction as the stock update, and skip anything you've already handled.

Still in the consumer, each item is updated on its own. If the third item fails, the first two stay decremented. It's safer to update the whole order in one transaction, and publish a failure event if any item can't be reserved.
Last, a small one. The down method is empty, so this migration can't be rolled back. Dropping the new column there would fix that.
To sum up: make the consumer idempotent and give the new column a default before merging. The other two are quick wins. Thanks!
